hints: Apply the binomial series expansion $(1 + u)^{1/2} = 1 + \dfrac{1}{2}u + \dfrac{(1/2)(-1/2)}{2!}u^2 + \dots$ with $u = -2x$.
Multiply the resulting polynomial by $(3 + x)$ and collect all terms up to and including $x^2$.
walkthrough:
Apply the binomial series expansion $(1 + u)^n = 1 + nu + \dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}u^2 + \dots$ with $n = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $u = -2x$:
$$(1 - 2x)^{1/2} = 1 + \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)(-2x) + \dfrac{\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}{2!}(-2x)^2 + \dots$$

Calculate each term of $(1 - 2x)^{1/2}$ step by step:
$$\text{Linear term} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)(-2x) = -x$$
$$\text{Quadratic term} = \dfrac{-\dfrac{1}{4}}{2}(4x^2) = \left(-\dfrac{1}{8}\right)(4x^2) = -\dfrac{1}{2}x^2$$
So:
$$(1 - 2x)^{1/2} = 1 - x - \dfrac{1}{2}x^2 + \dots$$

Multiply this series expansion by $(3 + x)$:
$$(3 + x)\left(1 - x - \dfrac{1}{2}x^2 + \dots\right) = 3\left(1 - x - \dfrac{1}{2}x^2\right) + x\left(1 - x - \dfrac{1}{2}x^2\right)$$

Expand each bracket up to the term in $x^2$:
$$3\left(1 - x - \dfrac{1}{2}x^2\right) = 3 - 3x - \dfrac{3}{2}x^2$$
$$x(1 - x) = x - x^2$$

Combine all like terms:
$$\text{Constant term} = 3$$
$$\text{Term in } x = -3x + x = -2x$$
$$\text{Term in } x^2 = -\dfrac{3}{2}x^2 - x^2 = -\dfrac{5}{2}x^2$$
